info.title: OE Commerce Store REST API
info.description:
Build a fully custom headless storefront - your own web app, mobile app, or POS - against a
            single OE Commerce store. Every endpoint below is namespaced under `/api/v1/store/...`. Building
            admin/back-office tooling instead? See [/docs/admin](/docs/admin).

            New here? [/guides/store](/guides/store) walks through getting a key, the anonymous cart
            session, and calling your first endpoints step by step - this page is the field-level reference
            to come back to afterward.

            ## Getting Started

            1. Click the **Authorize** button at the top of this page.
            2. Provide credentials:
               - **X-Commerce-Key** (always required) - your store's Store Access Key from Backoffice >
                 Settings > Application APIs. `pk_store_...` (publishable) is safe for browser/mobile code;
                 `sk_store_...` (secret) is server-to-server only and is rejected outright if a browser
                 Origin header is present.
               - **Bearer** (only for endpoints acting on a specific customer - Account, Orders, Wishlists,
                 etc.) - the token from **Auth > register** or **Auth > login**.

            Once authorized, you can explore and test all available endpoints directly from this interface.

            ## Anonymous Carts

            A guest cart is tracked by an `X-Session-Ref` header, not a cookie - the server generates one on
            your first request and echoes it back on every response after. Keep sending back whatever value
            you last received. Logging in carries that same cart forward onto the customer's account
            automatically, with no separate merge step.

            ## Errors

            Failures use RFC 9457 Problem Details (`application/problem+json`) with a stable `code` field
            for programmatic handling, e.g. `store_key_invalid`, `store_key_revoked`, `store_key_scope_denied`,
            `rate_limited`. A rejected *business* action (e.g. adding fewer than a product's minimum order
            quantity to the cart) instead comes back as HTTP 200 with `"success": false` and a human-readable
            `message` - always check `success` in the body, not just the HTTP status code.

            ## Rate Limits

            Requests are limited per Store Access Key (200/minute). The credential-stuffing surface
            (register/login/forgot-password/reset-password) is limited more tightly per caller IP (10 per 5
            minutes). A 429 response includes a `Retry-After` header.

get.summary:
Faceted/filtered product listing - the category/search results page. Falls back to a plain database
keyword query (no facets - those need Solr's index) when the store has no Solr instance configured,
or the configured one is unreachable, instead of surfacing an opaque 500. Callers can detect this via
the SearchDegraded flag on the response.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, unless overridden by the store's own SearchSettings.PageSize.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort order (defaults to the store's configured default sort).

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Optional comma-separated list of fields to include per product (e.g. ?fields=productId,name,skuCode,pricing) - trims FilterProductModel's field set for mobile/lightweight clients. Only applies to each item in "products"; paging/facets/total are always returned in full. Unknown field names are ignored rather than erroring.

post.summary:
The cart-to-order handoff - creates the order from the current cart. Storefront never collects
card details itself: on success, RequiresPayment/RedirectUrl tell the frontend whether anything
further is needed and, if so, the URL to send the browser to - that provider's own hosted payment
page, whether that's Stripe Checkout or one of the store's other configured gateways. Never an
embedded card form.

This moves money (or at least commits stock and creates an order) - mobile networks retry, so an
optional Idempotency-Key header is honoured (see IdempotentAttribute): the same key with the same
request replays the original response instead of creating a second order; the same key with a
different request is rejected (422) rather than silently creating a different order under a key
the client thinks it already used.

post.summary:
Exchanges a refresh token for a new access token, without requiring the (possibly already expired)
access token itself - the whole point of a refresh token is to work after the access token has
expired. Rotation + reuse detection: every successful refresh revokes the presented token and
issues a new one in the same family; presenting a token that's already been used (already revoked)
is treated as theft and revokes the entire family, forcing a full re-login.

AddCartItemResponseModel.description:
Response for adding a catalog or custom line item to the cart - shared by AddItem and AddCustomItem,
which return the identical shape. Success populates CartReference/DocumentLineId/Checksum/Cart; a
validation failure (e.g. stock/policy warnings) instead populates Message/Warnings on the same 200.

mainCartQty.description: Total qty for this line in the first table (your items), so we can show e.g. "2 of 5 from your items".

firstWarehouseQty.description: Qty that ships from the first (default) warehouse — for display in top table e.g. "3 ship from Cape Town".

fulfillmentTableRows.description:
Fulfillment split rows for the second table (branch/warehouse with delivery message, read-only qty).
Same product can appear here and in Items; only Items table allows qty change.

CategoryModel.description: A category tree node - only categories with products (directly or via a descendant) are included.

ClearCartResponseModel.description: Response for clearing the cart - success populates only Success; failure also populates the ErrorCode/ErrorMessage/ErrorParams triad.

returnUrl.description:
Where the frontend wants the shopper returned to after a redirect-based payment gateway.
Required when PaymentMethodName is Stripe - Stripe Checkout has no default to fall back to.

CreateOrderResponseModel.description:
Response to a successful (or failed) order creation. Storefront never collects card details itself -
every payment method is a redirect to that provider's own hosted page, so RequiresPayment/RedirectUrl
together tell the frontend exactly what to do next: nothing further, or navigate the browser to
RedirectUrl (a full-page redirect, not an iframe - most gateways refuse to be framed).

success.description: Always true - this endpoint never reveals whether the account exists.

hash.description: Password reset hash to pass to reset-password, present only when the account exists.

GetCategoriesResponseModel.description: The full category tree - see CatalogController.GetCategories.

GetOrderStatusResponseModel.description: A lightweight status-only view of an order - see OrdersController.GetOrderStatus.

documentRef.description:
Public reference - GET gift-registries/{DocumentRef} is anonymous (anyone with the link can
    view and buy from the registry, which is the whole point), so a frontend builds its own share link
    from this rather than a separate token.

purchaseStatus.description:
"None" (not yet claimed), "Processing", "Purchased", "Expired" - only meaningful once someone
    has started buying this item off the registry.

documentRef.description:
Public reference - GET gift-registries/{DocumentRef} is anonymous (anyone with the link can
    view and buy from the registry, which is the whole point), so a frontend builds its own share link
    from this rather than a separate token.

refreshToken.description:
Single-use token that exchanges for a new access token via POST refresh-token, even after
    this access token has expired. Store it securely - presenting it a second time after it's been used
    revokes the whole session's refresh chain.

MarkGiftRegistryItemRequest.description:
Records that a gift-giver (anyone with the registry link, not just its owner) is buying or has
    bought an item off someone else's registry.

wishlistId.description: Target wishlist. Omit to use the customer's first/default wishlist, creating "My Wishlist" if they have none.

PricingTiersResponseModel.description:
Quantity-break pricing table for one product - the headless equivalent of StoreApp's
    bulk/tiered pricing widget (ProductBulkPriceController), same underlying GetProductBulkPriceService data.

ProductsListResponseModel.description:
Shared response shape for the client-supplied-product-id-list endpoints (Compare/RecentlyViewed/Trending) -
documents the untrimmed FilterProductModel list shape; JsonFieldSelector.Apply still trims/renames the
actual wire payload per-request (?fields=, id/sku -> productId/skuCode), unchanged by this type.

refreshToken.description: The refresh token issued at login/register or by a previous refresh-token call.
The next refresh token in the rotation chain - the one just presented is now spent.

RemovePromoCodeResponseModel.description:
Same envelope as AddPromoCodeResponseModel except CartId - here sourced from ICartContext's Reference
(string) rather than CartId (int), so the two actions can't share a single model.

ReorderRequest.description: Omit Items entirely to reorder every line on the order at its original quantity.

hash.description: Password reset hash issued by forgot-password.

otp.description: One-time PIN, if email verification is enabled for this store.

success.description: Whether the password was reset successfully.

addressId.description: Use a saved address (logged-in customers). When set, the guest fields below are ignored.

StoreProblemDetails.description:
RFC 9457 Problem Details shape every Store error response actually returns at runtime -
HeadlessStoreControllerBase.ProblemResponse, StoreApiKeyMiddleware, the rate limiter, and
ProblemDetailsExceptionHandler all emit this same shape (see StartupExtensions.cs's documented error
contract). Exists purely so the OpenAPI spec - and therefore generated SDKs - have a typed error model
instead of "any"; not constructed directly anywhere (the real responses are hand-built anonymous objects
with the same field names).

SuccessResponseModel.description:
Bare acknowledgement shape (`{ "success": true }`) returned by Store actions that don't have any other
data to report back - shared instead of each controller building its own anonymous object, so the OpenAPI
spec (and therefore generated SDKs) can document a real type instead of nothing.

SwitchAccountResponseModel.description:
Covers both SwitchAccount outcomes on the same 200 - a bare acknowledgement when the login could not be
resolved for re-minting, or the full re-minted token when it could. Token/ExpiresIn are omitted from the
JSON entirely (not written as null) in the bare case, matching the original anonymous-object shapes.

email.description: Changing this also updates the login email used to sign in, after a uniqueness check.

UpdateProfileRequest.description: Only non-null fields are applied - omit anything the caller doesn't want to change.

documentRef.description:
Public reference for this wishlist - GET wishlists/{DocumentRef} is anonymous, so a frontend
    can build its own "share" link from this (e.g. {its own domain}/wishlist/share?wishlist={DocumentRef}) -
    there's no separate share token to mint, matching StoreApp's own share mechanism.

Public reference for this wishlist - GET wishlists/{DocumentRef} is anonymous, so a frontend
    can build its own "share" link from this (e.g. {its own domain}/wishlist/share?wishlist={DocumentRef}) -
    there's no separate share token to mint, matching StoreApp's own share mechanism.

X-Commerce-Key.description: Your store's Store Access Key, from Backoffice > Settings > Application APIs. Every request needs one. Two kinds: sk_store_... (secret - server-to-server only, rejected outright if a browser Origin header is present) and pk_store_... (publishable - safe to ship in browser/mobile code, the same way a Stripe publishable key is). A key can optionally be scoped to specific write permissions and restricted to an origin allowlist - see the same Backoffice screen.
X-Commerce-Key.name: X-Commerce-Key

Bearer.description: Customer access token from Auth > register or Auth > login. Required in addition to the Store Access Key for any endpoint acting on a specific customer (cart/checkout work without it, resolved instead from the X-Session-Ref header - see the document description).
